 Judgment

1. This is a statutory appeal under Jammu and Kashmir Land Acquisition Act, Svt. 1990 preferred by the appellant-Union of India through Estate Officer, Northern Command, Udhampur against a reference award dated 28.11.2003 passed by the court of learned Principal District Judge,
Udhampur on file no. 4/L.A. Act titled 'Bodh Raj and ors. Vs. Special Collector, Land Acquisition (Army) Udhampur'.
2.

sentences.text: Land measuring 32.16 kanals was in the private ownership of the respondents herein.
Said land was comprised in khasra nos. 600/84, 612/113 and 111 in village Kawa.
This land formed part of 1480 kanals and 07 marlas of land which came to be acquired on the requisition of D.E.O., Northern Command, Udhampur for the public purpose of extension air field.
4. The Collector

Land Acquisition (Army), Udhampur had assessed the compensation payable for the acquisition of the land and as per the assessment so made by the Collector, the compensation was payable @ Rs. 30,000/- per kanal for cultureable (warhal mandi) land and Rs. 20,000/- per kanal for un-cultureable (banjar kadim).
The acquisition of the land was held to be payable with jabrana @15% along with cost of Rs. 1,927/-.

Thus, the total land compensation payable to the petitioner for 32.16 kanals of land was held to be Rs. 10,56,477/- which was received by the respondents under protest seeking reference for the purpose of determination of correct market valuation of the land so acquired.

5. Reference came to be made under Section 18 of the Jammu and Kashmir Land Acquisition Act,
Svt. 1990 by the Special Collector Land Acquisition (Army), Udhampur vide his no. 153-55 LAD dated 11.11.1999.
6.

sentences.text: (i) Whether the petitioners whose lands have been acquired in village Kawa and in other adjoining villages, for the extension of Air Field, have not been paid compensation of the land as per the prevalent market rate?

(OPP) 
(ii) In case issue no. 1 is proved in affirmative, whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation at the rate of Rs.
50,000/- per kanal?

(OPP) 
7.

During the pendency of the reference proceedings, the original petitioners, namely, Prabhu Dayal and Krishan Lal who figured along with Bodh Rajh and Shiv Lal came to expire resulting in bringing on record their legal representatives and all of them are now figuring in the present appeal as respondents.
8.
The court of learned Principal District Judge, Udhampur came to deal with the aforesaid two issues upon the basis of the evidence which was led in the case.

9. The admitted state of facts which came before the reference court are that the acquired land is situated within the close vicinity of Udhampur town on Dhar Road, NHW, Udhampur and was having a big residential locality developed around it, thus, vesting the acquired land with economic potential and there were sale deeds of relevant time pertaining to the lands in the adjoining areas as well as acquisition awards made with respect to adjoining villages Sangroor and village Kashirah.
10.

The court of learned Principal District Judge, Udhampur came to take notice of an award passed by the same court on file no. 2/LAA dated 08.02.2003 in which the subject land was also the one covered by the same very declaration no. Rev. LAJ (89-87) dated 21.06.1989 issued in the same very village Kawa and acquired for the same very purpose of extension of air field, Udhampur.

11. By referring to the said reference, the court of learned Principal District Judge, Udhampur treated the present case on parity basis thereby enhancing the compensation to an amount of Rs.
50,000/- per kanal for cultureable land and Rs. 40,000/- for non-cultureable land and held the respondents entitled to 15% Jabrana plus interest @6% p.a from the date of their dispossession till the final payment of the compensation.

12. It is against this enhancement of compensation from Rs.
30,000/- to Rs. 50,000/- in case of cultureable land and from Rs. 20,000/- to Rs. 40,000/- in case of non-cultureable land that the appellant-Union of India has felt itself aggrieved to come in appeal challenging the enhancement on the basis that the estimate of compensation made by the Collector Land Acquisition in the case was on the basis of the market value prevailing at the relevant point of time which required no revision much less for higher side and that the evidence produced by the respondents was pertaining to smaller areas which could not have been made basis for the reference court to give enhancement to the compensation assessed by the Collector.

sentences.text: In addition, the appellant has pleaded that it was not heard by the learned Principal District Judge, Udhampur in the case as it did not figure as a party in the matter.
In this regard, the appellant has referred to the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court as cited in the memo of appeal.

14. Upon hearing the submissions from both the sides, this Court has no hesitation to acknowledge that the appellant as being the indenting department did not figure as a party respondent in the reference proceedings before the court of learned Principal District Judge, Udhampur and that could have an effect to undo the proceedings in the case but when this Court addresses its mind to the aspect that the matter relates back to the acquisition proceedings conducted in the year 1983,
this Court is left to opt between technicality or rationality of the situation.

15. Technicality would urge this Court to undo the exercise and refer the matter back to the court of learned Principal District Judge, Udhampur for de novo reference proceedings by joining the appellant as a party respondent whereas, the rationality would weigh with this Court to bring an end to this litigation which cannot outlast the life of the persons who came to be first associated with it in the form of the owners of the land.

In fact, the original claimants have demised even during the course of proceedings in reference case before the court of learned Principal District Judge,
Udhampur.
16. Thus, this Court is negating the plea of the appellant with respect to legality of the impugned award on the count of non- impleadment of the appellant as being the indenting department.

17. Now, with respect to the enhancement made by the reference court, the reference court in fact came to accord parity on account of the fact that in terms of an award dated 08.08.2003 in a matter on file no. 2/LAA, the court of learned Principal District Judge, Udhampur had already accorded enhancement in favour of the land owners as against the appellant herein when in the said case the land was acquired for the same very purpose and in fact part of the same very acquisition process relatable to same declaration no. Rev. LAJ (89-87) dated 21.06.1989.
18.
In the light of this, the present appeal is held to be meritless warranting no interference with the award appealed against.

The same is, accordingly, dismissed along with connected applications.
19. Record of the court below and Collector Land Acquisition, if called, be returned back.
( Rahul Bharti) Judge JAMMU 11.08.2023 Naresh, Secy.
